questions.title: ATM Menu Simulator
questions.description:
An ATM simulator processes a list of menu selections. Option 1 prints Balance 5000, option 2 prints Deposit noted, option 3 prints Withdrawal noted, and option 4 prints Session ended and stops the session immediately, ignoring all remaining selections. Any other option prints Invalid option and is skipped without ending the session. Read the number of selections and each selection, and simulate the session using break and continue inside the option loop.

Input Format:
First line: integer n, the number of scheduled selections. Next n lines: one integer option each.

Output Format:
One line per processed selection as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= option <= 9
questions.output1:
Withdrawal noted
Invalid option
Balance 5000
Deposit noted
questions.output3:
Balance 5000
Invalid option
Deposit noted
Invalid option
Withdrawal noted
Session ended

questions.title: ATM PIN Retry
questions.description:
An ATM asks for a PIN and keeps prompting until the correct one is entered. The first token of the input is the correct PIN, followed by the PINs the customer actually typed, in order; the last attempt always matches. Simulate the retries with a do-while loop (each attempt must be checked after it is read) and print which attempt number finally grants access.

Input Format:
The first token is the correct PIN. The remaining tokens are the entered PINs in order; the last of them equals the correct PIN.

Output Format:
One line: Access granted on attempt X, where X is the 1-based number of the matching attempt.

Constraints:
PIN strings of 1 to 8 digits, at most 5 attempts, the last attempt is correct
questions.inputconstrains: PIN strings of 1 to 8 digits, at most 5 attempts, the last attempt is correct

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Guard
questions.description:
An ATM must reject withdrawals that exceed the account balance. Read the balance and the requested amount. If the amount is larger than the balance, use throw to raise new IllegalArgumentException with the message 'Insufficient balance' and catch it in main; otherwise complete the withdrawal.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: balance and amount.

Output Format:
On success print two lines: 'Withdrawn: amount' and 'Remaining balance: newBalance'. If the request is rejected, print exactly one line: 'Transaction failed: Insufficient balance'.

Constraints:
0 <= balance, amount <= 1000000

questions.title: Abstract Notification System
questions.description:
A notification hub sends the same command to different channels. Define an abstract class Notification with an abstract method send(String message). Define EmailNotification extends Notification where send prints: EMAIL: <message>, and SMSNotification extends Notification where send prints: SMS: <message>. Read n notification lines, dispatch each through a Notification reference, and finish with the two count lines.

Input Format:
First line: one integer n. Then n lines, each: email <message> or sms <message> (the message may contain spaces).

Output Format:
One output line per notification in order, then the line Email total: <count of email notifications> and the line SMS total: <count of sms notifications>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= message length <= 200

questions.title: Abstract Shape Area Chooser
questions.description:
An abstract class states what every shape must do without saying how. Define an abstract class Shape with an abstract method area(). Define Circle extends Shape (field radius, area = Math.PI * radius * radius) and Rectangle extends Shape (fields width and height, area = width * height). Read one shape description, build the matching object through a Shape reference, and print its area. Writing new Shape() directly would not even compile, because abstract classes cannot be instantiated.

Input Format:
A single line: either circle r OR rect w h.

Output Format:
Print one line: the area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < r, w, h <= 10000

questions.title: Abstract Shape Concrete Circle
questions.description:
An abstract class defines what a shape can do; subclasses decide how. Define an abstract class Shape with a field radius, a concrete method describe() that prints: This is a shape, and an abstract method area(). Define class Circle that extends Shape and implements area() as Math.PI * radius * radius. In main, read the radius into a Circle object held in a Shape reference, call describe() and print the area with 2 decimals.

Input Format:
A single line with one number: the radius r.

Output Format:
Line 1: This is a shape
Line 2: Area: <area with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 < r <= 10000

questions.title: Age Setter Validation
questions.description:
A setter can refuse bad data instead of storing it. Define a class Person with a private int field age (default 0), a method setAge(int a) that stores a only when a >= 0 and otherwise prints Invalid age while keeping the previous value, and a method getAge(). In main, read n and then n candidate ages, call setAge for each in order, and finally print the current age using getAge().

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated integers (the candidate ages).

Output Format:
Print Invalid age for every rejected value (in order), then one final line with the current age.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000 <= candidate age <= 1000
questions.output1:
Invalid age
Invalid age
Invalid age
5

questions.title: Age Validator Checked Exception
questions.description:
Many real-world validations use custom checked exceptions so that callers cannot forget to handle them. Create a class InvalidAgeException that extends Exception and stores a detail message through super(message). Method checkAge(int age) declares 'throws InvalidAgeException' and throws it with message 'Invalid age: age' whenever age is below 18 or above 100. Catch it in main and report the failure using getMessage().

Input Format:
A single line with one integer: age.

Output Format:
Print 'Valid age: age' when 18 <= age <= 100. Otherwise print 'Error: Invalid age: age'.

Constraints:
0 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Aggregate Student Marks Alphabetically
questions.description:
Every line of a marks sheet names a student and the marks they scored on one assessment; a student may appear many times. Aggregate the totals per student, then print one line per student with their total, ordered alphabetically by name. A TreeMap keeps its keys sorted, which makes the output order automatic.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name marks.

Output Format:
One line per distinct student, alphabetically by name: name total.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= marks <= 100; names are single-word tokens

questions.title: Alternating Merge of Two Lists
questions.description:
A card shuffler merges two decks by alternately taking one card from each deck, starting with deck A, then appending whatever remains of the longer deck. Build both input sequences as ArrayList objects, produce the alternating merge into a new ArrayList, and print it.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers for list A. Third line: m. Fourth line: m space-separated integers for list B.

Output Format:
One line: 'Merged: ' followed by the merged list space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 100000; -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Anagram Check With Count Arrays
questions.description:
A crossword generator must verify that two words are anagrams: they use exactly the same letters with the same counts. Read two lowercase words and compare their letter counts using two integer arrays of size 26 (one slot per letter a to z). Do not sort the words and do not use maps.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated words, each without spaces.

Output Format:
Print anagram when the words are anagrams of each other, otherwise print not anagram.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Animal Speak Scoreboard
questions.description:
A pet show announcer reads the lineup into an Animal[] base array. Dog, Cat and Duck extend Animal and override speak() with their own sound. One loop then prints each animal's name and the sound returned through the base reference, letting dynamic method dispatch choose every override. Do not use switch or instanceof.

Input Format:
First line: n. Next n lines: kind name where kind is dog, cat or duck and name is one word.

Output Format:
One line per animal in order: name: Sound.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; names are single words

questions.title: App JVM Compatibility Checker
questions.description:
A deployment bot checks whether an app can run on the installed JVM before shipping. Read the app name, the JVM version the app requires and the installed JVM version. Print the check report; an upgrade is needed exactly when the installed version is lower than the required version.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens separated by spaces: app name (a single word), required JVM version (an integer), installed JVM version (an integer).

Output Format:
App: <app>
Required JVM: <required>
Installed JVM: <installed>
Upgrade needed: yes or no

1 <= required <= 100, 1 <= installed <= 100

questions.title: Array Access with Fallback
questions.description:
Reading past the end of an array throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Read n, then n integers into an array, and finally an index. Print the element stored at that index, or catch the exception and print a fallback message.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: the index to read.

Output Format:
Print 'Value: x' for a valid index. For any out-of-range index (including negative), print 'Error: Index out of range'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100 and each element satisfies -1000 <= x <= 1000. The index can be any integer.

questions.title: Array Sum with Enhanced For
questions.description:
Read n integers into an int array, then use an enhanced for loop (for(int v : array)) to compute and print their sum.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the array elements.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of all elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each element between -1000000 and 1000000

questions.title: Attendance Eligibility Count
questions.description:
A college allows students to sit for the exam only if their attendance is 75 percent or more. The office stored the attendance percentage of each student in an array. Count how many students are eligible (attendance >= 75) and how many are not.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of students.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the attendance percentages.

Output Format:
Line 1: Eligible: <count of students with attendance >= 75>
Line 2: Not eligible: <count of students with attendance < 75>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= attendance <= 100

questions.title: Bank Account Opening Balance
questions.description:
Silverline Bank opens a savings account by feeding the holder's name and the opening balance into a parameterized constructor. As a launch offer, the constructor itself adds a welcome bonus of 200 to any opening balance of 5000 or more. Define class SavingsAccount with fields holder and balance and a constructor SavingsAccount(String holder, int balance) that stores the holder and the (possibly bonus-boosted) balance. Read the values, create the account, and print both fields.

Input Format:
One line: holder balance (holder is a single word, balance is an integer).

Output Format:
Line 1: Holder: <holder>
Line 2: Balance: <balance after any bonus>

Constraints:
1 <= holder length <= 20, 0 <= balance <= 100000

questions.title: Bank Account Type Chooser
questions.description:
A bank offers two account flavors built on one base class - hierarchical inheritance. Define class Account with fields holder and balance. Define class SavingsAccount that extends Account with field rate and method addInterest() that adds balance * rate / 100 to balance. Define class CurrentAccount that extends Account with field fee and method applyFee() that subtracts fee from balance. In main read type (1 = savings, 2 = current), then holder, balance and the matching parameter, apply the operation, and print the holder and final balance with 2 decimals.

Input Format:
A single line: type holder balance param where type is 1 (param = rate) or 2 (param = fee); holder is one word.

Output Format:
Line 1: Holder: <holder>
Line 2: Balance: <final balance with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
type is 1 or 2, 0 < balance <= 1000000, 0 <= rate, fee <= 100000
questions.inputconstrains: type is 1 or 2, 0 < balance <= 1000000, 0 <= rate, fee <= 100000

questions.title: Bank Deposit Only Account
questions.description:
A new bank account starts empty. Define a class BankAccount with a private double field balance starting at 0.0, a method deposit(double amount) that adds to the balance, and a method getBalance() that returns it. In main, read n and then n deposit amounts, perform the deposits in order on one account object, and print the final balance.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated deposit amounts.

Output Format:
Print one line: the final balance rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= deposit amount <= 100000

questions.title: Bank Transaction Tally
questions.description:
A bank account keeps a private tally of every successful transaction. Define a class BankAccount with private fields balance, transactions, deposited and withdrawn (all starting at 0). deposit(double amount) always succeeds: it adds to balance, adds to deposited and increases transactions. withdraw(double amount) succeeds only when amount <= balance: it subtracts from balance, adds to withdrawn and increases transactions; otherwise it prints Rejected and changes nothing. Read n operations (D amount or W amount), apply them in order on one account object, then print the summary.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by an amount.

Output Format:
Print Rejected immediately for every failed withdrawal, then four summary lines: Balance: <2dp> / Transactions: <int> / Deposited: <2dp> / Withdrawn: <2dp>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Bank Withdraw Validation
questions.description:
With private data, the only way in is through the object's own rules. Define class BankAccount with a private double field balance, a method deposit(double amount) that adds it, a method withdraw(double amount) that subtracts only when amount <= balance and otherwise prints Insufficient funds, and a method getBalance(). Read n operations, apply them in order on one account, and print the final balance at the end.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by the amount.

Output Format:
Print Insufficient funds immediately for every rejected withdrawal (in order), then one final line: the balance rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000
questions.blacklist: public double balance, public int balance

questions.title: Banking Ledger Processor
questions.description:
A bank's nightly ledger replays transactions and must survive failures. Define two custom CHECKED exception classes, InsufficientFundsException and NegativeAmountException, both extending Exception with super(message). Read an initial balance, then process n operations: DEPOSIT x adds x (negative x raises NegativeAmountException with message 'Negative amount: x'), WITHDRAW x subtracts x (negative x raises NegativeAmountException; x above the balance raises InsufficientFundsException with message 'Insufficient funds: x'), and BALANCE prints the current balance. Each failed operation is caught, counted and reported, and the ledger keeps processing afterwards. At the end print the final balance and the number of failed operations.

Input Format:
First line: n and the initial balance. Each of the next n lines: an operation — 'DEPOSIT x', 'WITHDRAW x', or 'BALANCE'.

Output Format:
Per operation print 'Deposited: x', 'Withdrawn: x' or 'Balance: b'; for a caught failure print 'Rejected: message' instead. Then print two final lines: 'Final balance: b' and 'Failed operations: f'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= initial balance <= 1000000000, -1000000000 <= x <= 1000000000

A drawing app keeps one variable of the base type Shape. Depending on the input it stores a Circle or a Square in that same reference, then calls draw() exactly once. The version that runs is decided by the object's runtime class, not the reference type, which is dynamic method dispatch.

Input Format:
One line: kind value where kind is circle (radius, decimal) or square (side, decimal).

Output Format:
One line: Drawing a circle with radius R or Drawing a square with side S, with the number printed the way Java prints a double (e.g. 3.0).

kind is circle or square; 0.1 <= value <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: kind is circle or square; 0.1 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Batch Jobs with Guaranteed Cleanup
questions.description:
A CI runner executes n jobs one after another, and every job must release its resources — even when it fails mid-run. For each job line (name code): inside try print 'Open name' and, when code is negative, throw new IllegalArgumentException with message 'Bad code: code'; otherwise print 'Run name'. The catch prints 'Error in name: Bad code: code' and counts the failure, while the finally block ALWAYS prints 'Close name'. After all jobs print the success and failure counts.

Input Format:
First line: n. Each of the next n lines: a job name (no spaces) and an integer code.

Output Format:
Per job, in order: 'Open name', then 'Run name' or 'Error in name: Bad code: code', then 'Close name'. Final two lines: 'Successful jobs: s' and 'Failed jobs: f'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, job name length 1 <= len <= 30, -1000 <= code <= 1000

questions.title: Batch Sum Reducer
questions.description:
A reporting engine splits a dataset of k chunks of m values each across k worker tasks; every task is an object implementing Runnable that sums its chunk into its own slot and then reports it through one synchronized merge method that also grows the grand total. First line: k and m. Second line: k * m space-separated values.

Output Format:
k lines 'Chunk i: sum' in chunk order, then 'Grand total: g'.

1 <= k <= 6, 1 <= m <= 20, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: BiFunction Operation Chooser
questions.description:
A geometry panel lets users pick an operation by name and applies it to two operands. Store the named operations in a map as BiFunction<Double, Double, Double> lambdas (add, sub, mul) and dispatch with map.get instead of a switch statement.

Input Format:
One line: an operation (add, sub or mul) followed by two decimals.

Output Format:
Print the result with exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-10000 <= operands <= 10000; op is add, sub or mul

questions.title: Bike Odometer Rides
questions.description:
A bike's odometer grows with every ride. Define a class Bike with a field odometer starting at 0, a method ride(int km) that adds km to the odometer, and a method getOdometer() that returns it. In main, read n and then n km values, call ride for each value on one Bike object, and print the final odometer reading.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated integers (the km of each ride).

Output Format:
Print one line: the total odometer reading.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= km <= 10000

questions.title: Binary Representation Using Recursion
questions.description:
A satellite telemetry tool must show an equipment ID as a binary pattern. Write a recursive method printBinary(int n) that prints the binary form of n without leading zeros by recursing on n / 2 first and printing n % 2 after the call returns, so the most significant bit is printed first. No loops, and the built-in Integer.toBinaryString is banned.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the binary representation of n without leading zeros.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Binary Search on a Shelf Using Recursion
questions.description:
A library search terminal must locate a book code on a shelf whose codes are sorted in strictly increasing order. Implement binary search as pure recursion: a recursive readValues(Scanner, index, n) method fills the array one element per call, and a recursive binarySearch(low, high, key) halves the range each call, returning the 0-based index where the key was found or -1 when it is absent. The program must contain no for and no while statements, so reading the input is recursive too.

Input Format:
A single line with n followed by n strictly increasing sorted integers followed by the key to find.

Output Format:
Print one line: the 0-based index of the key, or -1 if it is not on the shelf.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bitwise Playground

One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Print six lines: a & b, then a | b, then a ^ b, then ~a, then a << 1, and finally a >> 1.

0 <= a, b <= 100000.

questions.title: Border Elements in Clockwise Order

A perimeter alarm system inspects only the border cells of a field grid, in clockwise order: first the entire top row left to right, then the right column top to bottom, then the bottom row right to left, then the left column bottom to top. Read r and c, then the r x c grid, and print all border values on one line separated by single spaces in that order.

Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
One line: the border values in clockwise order separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 100, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Bounded Buffer Order Fulfiller

Output Format:
k lines 'Consumed: x' in consumption order, then 'Total consumed: k'.

1 <= cap <= 3, 1 <= k <= 6, 1 <= item <= 100

Print 'Max: v' where v is the largest value.

1 <= n <= 100; each value is between -1000000 and 1000000

questions.title: Box Arity Constructor Choice

One line containing either one integer side, or two integers length width.

One line: Volume: <volume>

the line has 1 or 2 integers, each 1..1000

questions.title: Box Creation History Counter
questions.description:
A factory tracks how its boxes are built. Every Box constructor must count itself: the default constructor increments a static counter for default builds, the parameterized constructor increments a static counter for sized builds, and the copy constructor increments a static counter for copies. An event desk automates conference badges with a Java program. Read the attendee name, badge number and event code, then print the badge. The seat pass line is formed by joining the event code, a hyphen and the badge number.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens separated by spaces: name (a single word), badge number (an integer), event code (a single word).

Output Format:

CONFERENCE BADGE
Name: <name>
Badge No: <badge>

Seat pass: <eventCode>-<badge>

questions.title: Conference Visitor Analytics
questions.description:
A conference gate logs attendee names, one entry per scan. Produce an analytics report: the deduplicated names in the order they first appeared (a LinkedHashSet preserves first-appearance order), the number of unique attendees, and for q requested names the number of times each appears in the original log. Count occurrences by scanning the original log list, not with any key-value map.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated names. Third line: q. Each of the next q lines contains one name to count.

Output Format:
First line: 'First appearances: ' followed by the deduplicated names space-separated. Second line: 'Unique: ' followed by the number of unique names. Then one line per query: 'name: count' where count is how many times name occurs in the log (0 is possible).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= q <= 100; names are single words of length 1 to 20

One line with one integer: the Celsius temperature.

Output Format:
Celsius: <celsius>
Freezing point: 0
Boiling point: 100

questions.title: Contact Book Manager
questions.description:
Manage a phone contact book backed by a HashMap. ADD name number stores a contact and prints Added; FIND name prints the stored number or Not found; DELETE name prints Deleted when the contact existed (and removes it) or Not found; COUNT prints how many contacts are stored.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q.
Next q lines: one query each: ADD name number, FIND name, DELETE name or COUNT.

Output Format:
One line for every query.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; names and numbers are single-word tokens; numbers have up to 10 digits

questions.title: Contest Leaderboard Top-K
questions.description:
A coding contest leaderboard receives score updates; every update names a player and sets their current total score (a later update for the same player replaces the earlier score). After reading all updates and a number k, print the top k players ordered by score descending; players with equal scores are ordered alphabetically by name. Aggregate latest scores in a TreeMap, then sort the names with a two-level comparator.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name score.
Next line: the integer k.

Output Format:
k lines: name score, from highest score to lowest, alphabetical for ties.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= number of distinct names <= n <= 100000; 0 <= score <= 1000000000

questions.title: Copy Array and Print
questions.description:
Read n integers into a source array. Then create a second array of the same length and copy every element of the source into it with a loop (element by element, not by assigning references). Print both arrays on separate lines.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: Original: followed by the source elements separated by single spaces.
Line 2: Copy: followed by the copied elements separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Corner Shop Receipt
questions.description:
A corner shop uses a tiny Java program to print receipt slips for every sale. Read the item name and the quantity sold, then print the slip. The shop also tracks a restock level, computed as quantity + 10.

Input Format:
One line with the item name (a single word) and an integer quantity, separated by a space.

Output Format:
*** RECEIPT ***
Item: <item>
Quantity: <quantity>
Restock level: <quantity + 10>

Constraints:
1 <= quantity <= 500

questions.title: Count Chars In Notes
questions.description:
Before sending a notes file over a slow link, an app checks its exact size on disk. Each word is written to notes.txt on its own line using println, which appends one newline character after the word, so the file holds len(word) + 1 characters per word.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated words (letters only).

Output Format:
After writing, ask the File object for its size and print 'Chars: L' where L is the file length in characters.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20 and each word has 1 to 20 letters

questions.title: Count Matching Values
questions.description:
A survey tool counts how many readings satisfy a rule chosen at runtime. Write a generic method declared as public static <T> int countMatching(T[] arr, Predicate<T> pred) and call it with a lambda that tests whether a value is strictly greater than a threshold. Do not use streams.

Input Format:
One line: n, threshold, then n integers.

Output Format:
Print 'Count: c' where c is how many values are strictly greater than threshold.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000000 <= values and threshold <= 1000000

questions.title: Count Vowels in a Word Using a Method
questions.description:
Write a program with a static method countVowels that receives a word as a parameter and returns how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u in lower or upper case) the word contains. Read the word in main, call the method, and print the returned count.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the number of vowels in the word.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, letters only

questions.title: Count the Digits
questions.description:
Read an integer n and count how many digits it has using a while loop that divides the number by 10 repeatedly until it becomes 0.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of digits.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000000000

questions.title: Covariant Produce Demo
questions.description:
An animal shelter hands out pets. The base class Shelter has adopt(String name) that returns an Animal. DogShelter overrides adopt with a covariant return type Dog, and CatShelter overrides it to return Cat, so callers get the specific type without any cast. Read the kind and a name, adopt from the matching shelter, and print what the animal says plus one extra behaviour line for dogs and cats.

Input Format:
One line: kind name where kind is dog, cat or any.

Output Format:
For dog: name says Woof then name fetches the ball. For cat: name says Meow then name purrs softly. For any: only name says Grr.

Constraints:
kind is dog, cat or any; 1 <= name length <= 20
questions.inputconstrains: kind is dog, cat or any; 1 <= name length <= 20

questions.title: Covariant Shape Factory
questions.description:
A drawing app builds shapes through factories. Base class ShapeFactory has produce() returning a Shape. CircleFactory overrides produce() with a covariant return type Circle and SquareFactory with Square, so main can hold the produced object in the specific type without any cast. Read the kind and value, produce from the matching factory, and print the description and area.

Input Format:
One line: kind value where kind is circle (radius) or square (side), decimals allowed.

Output Format:
Line 1: Produced: circle with radius R or Produced: square with side S (number printed the plain Java double way, e.g. 3.0). Line 2: Area: A with 2 decimals.

Constraints:
kind is circle or square; 0.1 <= value <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: kind is circle or square; 0.1 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Credential Validator
questions.description:
A login service checks credentials with two rules before granting access. Using Predicate lambdas, verify that the username has at least 4 characters and the password has at least 6 characters, and grant access only when both rules pass.

Input Format:
One line: a username token and a password token.

Output Format:
Print 'Access granted' if both checks pass, otherwise 'Access denied'.

Constraints:
Username and password are single tokens of 1 to 20 characters
questions.inputconstrains: username and password are single tokens of 1-20 characters

questions.title: Currency Note Splitter
questions.description:
A bank cashier program splits a withdrawal amount into 500 and 100 rupee notes. Read the amount and print how many notes of each denomination are handed out and what remainder is left (always less than 100).

Input Format:
One line with one integer: the amount.

Output Format:
Amount: <amount>
500 x <amount / 500>
100 x <remainder / 100>
Left: <remainder % 100>

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Daily Temperature Log Statistics
questions.description:
A weather station logged the temperature of n consecutive days as integers. Analyze the log: print the hottest temperature, the coldest temperature, and the average temperature rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of days.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the temperatures.

Output Format:
Line 1: Hottest: <value>
Line 2: Coldest: <value>
Line 3: Average: <value rounded to exactly 2 decimal places>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= temperature <= 1000000

questions.title: Date Validator and Weekday Finder
questions.description:
A legacy calendar service validates a date and reports its weekday without using any date library. First the month must be 1 to 12, otherwise print Invalid month. Then the day must fit the month, where February has 29 days in a leap year (a year divisible by 4 and not by 100, or divisible by 400); otherwise print Invalid date. For a valid date compute the weekday with Zeller's congruence: shift January and February to months 13 and 14 of the previous year, let k be the adjusted year % 100 and j the adjusted year / 100, then h = (day + (13 * (m + 1)) / 5 + k + k / 4 + j / 4 + 5 * j) % 7 where h = 0 means Saturday, 1 Sunday, 2 Monday, 3 Tuesday, 4 Wednesday, 5 Thursday and 6 Friday. Print the weekday name using a switch.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers: year, month and day.

Output Format:
Print the weekday name (Monday to Sunday), or Invalid month, or Invalid date.

Constraints:
1900 <= year <= 2100; 0 <= month <= 13; 0 <= day <= 32

questions.title: Days in Month with Grouped Cases
questions.description:
A calendar module prints the number of days in a month of a non-leap year using grouped case labels: months 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12 have 31 days; months 4, 6, 9 and 11 have 30; February has 28. Each group ends with break so control leaves the switch after exactly one print — omitting a break would let cases fall through and print wrong results. Read a month number and print its day count.

Input Format:
A single integer month.

Output Format:
Print 31, 30 or 28, or Invalid month when the value is not 1 to 12.

Constraints:
0 <= month <= 15

questions.title: Decimal to Binary via Shifts
questions.description:
A low-level tool shows a number in base 2 without using Integer.toBinaryString: it starts from a single 1-bit flag shifted left until it sits above the highest set bit, then walks the flag down while printing one bit at a time. It also previews two shift results.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer n.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Binary: B' with no leading zeros (just 0 when n is 0). Line 2: 'Doubled: X' which is n << 1. Line 3: 'Halved: Y' which is n >> 1.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000.

questions.title: Diagonal Difference of a Square Matrix
questions.description:
A math helper computes the diagonal difference of a square matrix: the absolute value of (sum of the main diagonal) minus (sum of the anti-diagonal). The main diagonal runs top-left to bottom-right; the anti-diagonal runs top-right to bottom-left. Read r and c (r = c), then the matrix, accumulate both diagonal sums as long values, and print one line with the absolute difference. Compute the absolute value with a simple comparison, not Math.abs.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c with r = c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
One line: the absolute difference between the two diagonal sums.

Constraints:
1 <= r = c <= 100, -1000000000 <= element <= 1000000000

questions.title: Digit Frequency Report
questions.description:
An auditor examines an account number and counts how many times each digit 0-9 occurs inside it. Extract the digits with a do-while loop (so the number 0 is also handled correctly), then print one line for every digit that occurs at least once, in ascending digit order.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
For each digit d that occurs in n, in ascending digit order: Digit d: count

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000000

questions.title: Digit Pyramid
questions.description:
Print a centered digit pyramid with n rows. Row i starts with (n - i) leading spaces, then the digits 1 to i in ascending order, then the digits i - 1 down to 1. The leading spaces are part of the output and must be printed exactly.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
n lines forming the pyramid.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 9

questions.title: Digit Sum Using Recursion
questions.description:
Write a recursive method digitSum that returns the sum of the digits of a non-negative number using recursion: digitSum(n) = (n % 10) + digitSum(n / 10), with the base case returning n itself once n is a single digit. Read n in main and print the returned digit sum.

Input Format:
A single line containing one non-negative integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the sum of the digits of n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000

questions.title: Discount Engine Overload Resolution
questions.description:
An online store's discount engine resolves three overload shapes of one method name. DiscountEngine has apply(double amount, int percent) cutting percent percent, apply(double amount, double fraction) cutting the given fraction, and apply(double amount, String code) where code FEST means 25 percent off (amount * 0.75), MEGA means half price (amount * 0.5), and any other word means no discount. Read the amount and the discount kind, call the matching overload, and print exactly which overload the compiler resolved plus the final price.

Input Format:
One line: amount kind value where kind is percent (integer), fraction (decimal) or code (single word).

Output Format:
One line: Int percent overload: P, Double fraction overload: P or String code overload: P, with P printed with 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0.1 <= amount <= 1000000; 1 <= percent <= 90; 0 <= fraction <= 0.9

questions.title: Distinct Window Report
questions.description:
A network monitor watches a stream of packet type ids and reports, for every window of k consecutive packets, how many distinct packet types it contains. Slide the window from left to right across the stream; for each of the n-k+1 windows, rebuild a HashSet from the window's packets and record its size.

Input Format:
First line: n and k space-separated. Second line: n space-separated integers (packet types).

Output Format:
One line: 'Windows: ' followed by n-k+1 counts space-separated (distinct packet types per window, left to right).

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 2000; -1000000 <= packet <= 1000000

questions.title: Dog Extends Animal Demo
questions.description:
Inheritance lets one class reuse another's members. Define a class Animal with a field name and a method eat() that prints: <name> eats food. Define a class Dog that extends Animal and adds a method bark() that prints: <name> barks. In main, read the dog's name, store it in a Dog object, then call eat() (inherited from Animal) and bark() (defined in Dog itself).

Input Format:
A single line with one word: the dog's name.

Output Format:
Line 1: <name> eats food
Line 2: <name> barks

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50

questions.title: Drain a Min-Heap PriorityQueue
questions.description:
Practice the two core PriorityQueue habits: adding elements and draining them. Read n distinct integers, insert every one into a PriorityQueue, then repeatedly poll the queue and print each removed element. With natural ordering the polled values come out in ascending order.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
One line per polled element, in the order they are removed (ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000

questions.title: Drawable Studio Render Engine
questions.description:
A drawing engine combines both blueprints from today: an abstract base class for shared state and an interface for the render contract. Define interface Drawable with void draw() and double area(). Define abstract class Shape with field name, a constructor Shape(String name) and an abstract method area(). Define Circle that extends Shape implements Drawable (area = Math.PI * r * r; draw() prints: Render circle area <area with 2 decimals>) and Square that extends Shape implements Drawable (area = s * s; draw() prints: Render square area <area with 2 decimals>). Input gives n shapes (circle radius or square side). Store them in a Drawable array, call draw() on each, then print the total area.

Input Format:
First line: n. Then n entries: circle radius OR square side (values may be decimals).

Output Format:
One line per shape as produced by draw(). Final line: Total area: <sum with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 < radius, side <= 10000

questions.title: EMI Calculator with Helper Methods
questions.description:
A bank wants a small EMI calculator built with modular methods. Write a static method monthlyRate(annualPercent) that returns the annual rate divided by 12 and then by 100, and a static method emi(principal, annualPercent, months) that returns the monthly installment using the reducing-balance formula: EMI = P * r * (1 + r)^n / ((1 + r)^n - 1), where r is the monthly rate and n is the number of months. Use Math.pow for the power. Read principal, annual rate and months in main and print the returned EMI rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: principal (number), annual rate in percent (number) and months (integer).

Output Format:
Print the EMI rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= principal <= 10000000, 0.1 <= rate <= 60, 1 <= months <= 360

questions.title: Electricity Bill Slab Calculator
questions.description:
A city bills electricity in slabs: the first 100 units cost 3.50 per unit, the next 100 units cost 5.00 per unit, and every unit above 200 costs 8.00 per unit. Accumulate the bill with compound assignment using relational comparisons.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer units.

Output Format:
Print one line: the bill amount to exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 5000.

questions.title: Electricity Bill with Slab Methods
questions.description:
A power company computes monthly bills with slab rates using modular methods. Write three static methods that each return a double: firstSlab(units) charging 3.50 per unit for the first 100 units, secondSlab(units) charging 4.60 per unit for units from 101 to 200, and thirdSlab(units) charging 6.50 per unit for units above 200. Write a fourth static method totalBill(units) that returns the sum of the three slab charges. Read the units consumed in main and print the returned total rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer: units consumed.

Output Format:
Print the total bill rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= units <= 100000

questions.title: Electricity Surcharge Calculator
questions.description:
A state electricity board adds a surcharge that depends on both the units consumed and the connection type. For units above 500 the surcharge is 250 for a commercial connection and 150 for a domestic one; for units above 200 it is 100 for commercial and 50 for domestic; at 200 units or below there is no surcharge. Read the units and the connection type and print the surcharge using nested ifs.

Input Format:
One line with an integer units and a token type (domestic or commercial).

Output Format:
Print the surcharge as an integer.

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 1000; type is domestic or commercial

questions.title: Event Bus Dispatch
questions.description:
A smart home hub lets users register handlers for event names and later fires events through them. Build a Map<String, Consumer<String>> of handlers: upper prints 'UPPER: s' with the message capitalized, reverse prints 'REVERSE: s' with the message reversed using a manual loop (no StringBuilder.reverse), and echo prints 'ECHO: s'. Fire each event by dispatching through map.get, not a switch statement.

Input Format:

A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

'Result: q' for each processed pair. 'Error: / by zero' if a division failed. Exactly one final line 'Cleanup done' in every case.

1 <= n <= 1000 and -1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000

Define a class Patient with private fields name (String), age (int) and admitted (boolean), setters setName/setAge/setAdmitted and getters getName/getAge/isAdmitted; setName also marks the patient as admitted. Read n events: admit name age creates and stores a Patient object in a Patient[] array; discharge name finds the first still-admitted patient with that name and marks them discharged. At the end print four lines: Admitted: <number of admit events>, Discharged: <number of successful discharges>, Still in ward: <patients not discharged>, Oldest: <name of the oldest patient still admitted (age)> or Oldest: None when nobody remains.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n events, each written as admit name age or discharge name.

Output Format:
Four lines exactly as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= age <= 120, 1 <= name length <= 50; every discharge name was admitted earlier and not discharged before

questions.description:
A hospital emergency room gives every arriving patient a token; a smaller token number means the patient is seen earlier, and all tokens are distinct. Process the shift log: ARRIVE name token queues a patient, NEXT prints the name of the next patient without serving them, SERVE serves and prints the name of the next patient, COUNT prints how many patients are still waiting. With nobody waiting, NEXT and SERVE print No patients.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q.
Next q lines: one query each: ARRIVE name token, NEXT, SERVE or COUNT.

Output Format:
One line for every NEXT, SERVE and COUNT query; ARRIVE produces no output.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; tokens are distinct positive integers <= 1000000; names are single words

questions.title: Image Brightness Inverter
questions.description:
An image editor inverts the brightness of a grayscale photo: every pixel value p (0 to 255) becomes 255 - p, which is a subtraction applied to every element of the pixel matrix. Read r and c, then r rows of c pixel values into a 2D array, invert every value, and print the new image row by row with values separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each (0 to 255).

Output Format:
r lines, each with the c inverted values of that row separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 100, 0 <= pixel <= 255

questions.title: In-Place Transpose of a Square Matrix
questions.description:
A graphics library needs the transpose of a square matrix computed in place. Read r and c (r = c), then the matrix into a 2D array, swap a[i][j] with a[j][i] for every pair of positions above the main diagonal (no second array needed), and print the transposed matrix row by row with values separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c with r = c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
r lines, each with the c values of the transposed row separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= r = c <= 100, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Increment Decrement Trace
questions.description:
Trace pre-increment, post-increment, pre-decrement and post-decrement on two variables. The postfix forms yield the old value; the prefix forms yield the new value.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Let x start as a and y start as b. Print five lines: the value of x++, then ++x, then y--, then --y, and finally x + y.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 100.

questions.title: Initialize and Print an Array
questions.description:
Create an array from user input and display it. Read n, then read n integers into an int array, and print all elements of the array on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n array elements separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Initials From a Full Name
questions.description:
An email generator builds a person's initials from their full name. Read the full name (words separated by single spaces) and print the first character of every word joined together.

Input Format:
A single line containing 2 to 5 words separated by single spaces, each word starting with a letter.

Output Format:
Print one line: the initials, one character per word in order.

Constraints:
2 <= number of words <= 5, 1 <= length of each word <= 20, letters only

questions.title: Insert at Index versus Append
questions.description:
list.add(x) appends at the end, but list.add(pos, x) inserts at index pos and shifts the following elements right by one. Read n integers into an ArrayList, then read an insertion position pos and a value v, insert v at index pos, and print the final list.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: pos and v space-separated.

Output Format:
One line: 'Result: ' followed by the final list space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= pos <= n; -1000000 <= v <= 1000000

questions.title: Integer vs Double Division
questions.description:
Integer division truncates the fraction, while converting an operand to double first keeps it. Read two integers a and b, then print a / b as plain integer division and (double) a / b formatted to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b separated by a space.

Output Format:
Int division: <a / b>
Double division: <(double) a / b with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
-100000 <= a <= 100000, 1 <= b <= 1000

questions.title: Inventory Deltas After Reload
questions.description:
A warehouse syncs stock with a central server through a serialized snapshot: the ArrayList of Product records (id, name, qty) is written to inventory.dat, then loaded back from disk, and the stock deltas received afterwards are applied to the LOADED objects before the corrected inventory is printed sorted by id.

Input Format:
First line: n. Then n lines, each with an integer id, a name (single word), and an integer qty. Then a line with d. Then d lines, each with an id and an integer delta (ids refer to stored products; a delta may be negative).

Output Format:
Serialize the list, deserialize it from inventory.dat, apply every delta to the matching product of the deserialized list, sort the products by id ascending, and print one line per product 'id name qty'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= d <= 50; ids are unique in 1..1000; 0 <= qty <= 100000; -100000 <= delta <= 100000 and every final qty stays >= 0
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, d <= 50; unique ids 1..1000; final qty >= 0

questions.title: Inventory Quantity Guard
questions.description:
Unchecked custom exceptions keep call sites clean because no throws declaration is required. Create a class InvalidQuantityException that extends RuntimeException. The method placeOrder(int quantity) throws it with message 'Invalid quantity: q' when quantity is zero or negative, and otherwise prints the confirmation. Handle the failure in main.

Input Format:
A single line with one integer: quantity.

Output Format:
Print 'Order placed for q units' when quantity >= 1. Otherwise print 'Order rejected: Invalid quantity: q'.

Constraints:
-1000 <= quantity <= 1000

questions.title: Invoice Line Total Method
questions.description:
A shopkeeper bills items using a small program. Write a static method lineTotal that receives the quantity, the unit price and a boolean discount flag as parameters and returns the line total as a double. The total is quantity times unit price; when the discount flag is true, reduce the total by 10 percent. Read the inputs in main, build the boolean flag, and print the returned total rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: quantity (integer), unit price (number) and discount flag (1 for discount applied, 0 for no discount).

Output Format:
Print the line total rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= quantity <= 10000, 0 < unit price <= 100000, flag is 0 or 1
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= quantity <= 10000, 0 < unit price <= 100000, flag is 0 or 1

questions.title: Invoice Total With Super
questions.description:
A billing system computes invoice totals. Base class Invoice stores item amounts and has subtotal() summing them plus total() returning subtotal(). TaxInvoice extends Invoice and overrides total(): it first takes super.total() as the base amount, then adds taxPercent percent of that base on top. Read the invoice kind, item amounts and tax percent, then print the subtotal and the dispatched total().

Input Format:
One line: kind n amount1 ... amountn taxPercent where kind is tax or plain (plain always has taxPercent 0).

Output Format:
Line 1: Subtotal: X (2 decimals). Line 2: Grand total: Y (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= item amounts <= 100000; 0 <= taxPercent <= 50

questions.title: Iterator Walk Over Words

First line: n. Second line: n space-separated words.

Output Format:
One word per line, in list order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; each word has length 1 to 20

A single line containing one integer n, the starting bottle count.

One line per count from n down to 1, with bottle singularized for the count 1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 99

A weather sensor gateway receives n distinct readings but has room to remember only the k most extreme ones. k lines: the k largest values in descending order, one per line.

1 <= k <= n <= 100000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000000

-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000; b is never 0 when op is /

Read the mode token: B means default constructor, C means read a model word and two integers and use the parameterized constructor. Print the spec card.

One line: either B, or C followed by model ram storage.

Line 1: Model: <model>

Line 3: Storage: <storage>GB

One line per countdown value from n down to 1, followed by the line Liftoff!.

A single line containing one integer n, the countdown start.

The numbers n down to 1, each on its own line, then the line Liftoff!

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100

Line 1: n and k, space separated.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the box order.

One line with the array after rotating left by k, separated by single spaces.

1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= n, -1000000000 <= element <= 1000000000

questions.title: Private Helper Messages

Public methods often delegate the real work to private helpers, hiding the details from callers. Define a class Greeter with a private method buildMessage(String name, int number) that returns Hello, <name>! You are visitor number <number>. and a method greet(String name, int number) that prints whatever buildMessage returns. In main, read n names and, for each i from 1 to n, call greet with the name and i. The helper stays private; only greet is called from outside the class.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated names (single words).

Output Format:
Print n lines in order: Hello, <name>! You are visitor number <i>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= name length <= 50
questions.sampleoutput1:
Hello, Asha! You are visitor number 1.
Hello, Vikram! You are visitor number 2.
questions.sampleoutput2: Hello, Meena! You are visitor number 1.
questions.output1:
Hello, Om! You are visitor number 1.
Hello, Max! You are visitor number 2.
Hello, Sid! You are visitor number 3.
questions.output2: Hello, Zoya! You are visitor number 1.
questions.output3:
Hello, Kiran! You are visitor number 1.
Hello, Riya! You are visitor number 2.

questions.title: Product Catalog Constructor Fit
questions.description:
A stockroom builds its catalog by handing each item to the smallest constructor that fits the data given: a bare name uses Product(String name) leaving price and qty at 0, a name with a price uses Product(String name, int price) leaving qty at 0, and a name with price and quantity uses Product(String name, int price, int qty). Define class Product with fields name, price, qty and these three overloaded constructors. Read n, then read n item lines (each with 1, 2 or 3 space-separated values) and build each product with the fitting constructor. Finally print every item.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: a name, or name price, or name price qty.

Output Format:
n lines, one per product: Item: <name>, Price: <price>, Qty: <qty>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= name length <= 20; 0 <= price <= 10000; 0 <= qty <= 1000

Item: Notebook, Price: 45, Qty: 0

Item: Brush, Price: 30, Qty: 5
questions.output3:

Item: Tape, Price: 0, Qty: 0

questions.title: Product Catalog Export
questions.description:
A shopkeeper backs up the day's catalog: an ArrayList of Serializable Product records (id, name, price, Comparable by id) is exported to catalog.dat with one writeObject call, and the export is verified by checking the file on disk.

Input Format:
First line: n. Then n lines, each with an integer id, a name (single word), and an integer price.

Output Format:
After serializing the list, print one line per product 'id name price', then 'Items: n', then 'Export ready: true' when catalog.dat exists and is not empty.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= id <= 9999; name is 1 to 15 letters; 1 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Product Code Formatter
questions.description:
A warehouse scanner emits product codes wrapped in stray spaces. Clean the raw line by trimming leading and trailing spaces, then print the code in uppercase. Spaces inside the code (if any) must be kept.

Input Format:
A single line containing the raw product code, possibly with leading and trailing spaces (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Print one line: the trimmed code converted to uppercase.

Constraints:
1 <= length of raw line <= 200

questions.title: Product Inventory Total Value
questions.description:
A storeroom holds many products, each with its own quantity and price. Define a class Product with fields name (String), quantity (int) and price (double), and a method stockValue() returning quantity * price. Read n products, create one Product object per record with new and keep them all in a Product[] array, then walk the array once and print each product's stock value, and finally the total value of the whole inventory.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n records, each written as name quantity price (name is one word).

Output Format:
Print n lines: <name> <stock value with 2 decimals> in input order, then one final line: Total: <total value with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= quantity <= 100000, 0 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Product Stock Update
questions.description:
A shopkeeper tracks one product's stock. Define a class Product with a field stock and methods buy(int qty) that adds qty, sell(int qty) that removes qty only when enough stock exists (a sell that would make stock negative is silently ignored), and getStock(). In main, read the initial stock and n operations, apply each B (buy) or S (sell) operation on one Product object, and print the final stock.

Input Format:
A single line: initialStock n followed by n operations, each written as the letter B or S followed by a quantity.

Output Format:
Print one line: the final stock.

Constraints:
0 <= initialStock <= 10000, 1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= qty <= 10000

questions.title: Purge and Patch Through the Iterator
questions.description:
An event processor walks a list of numeric event codes exactly once, using an Iterator for every removal. Rule 1: codes divisible by 2 are faulty and must be deleted via it.remove(). Rule 2: codes that survive and are divisible by 3 must be patched in place to three times their value. Rule 3: every other code is untouched. Removals change positions, so track the current index carefully when patching. Report the final list and the number of removed codes.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
First line: 'Kept: ' followed by the final list space-separated. Second line: 'Removed: ' followed by the number of removed codes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; -1000000 <= code <= 1000000

questions.title: Quiz Bank Grows On Disk
questions.description:
A quiz engine grows its bank on disk in two phases: first the Quiz object (holding a Question array) is serialized to quiz.dat, then a new question arrives and the enlarged quiz is serialized over the same file. Both classes are Serializable and Comparable (questions by qid, quizzes by size), and loading the file back must show the grown bank, proving the second save replaced the first.

Input Format:
First line: m. Then m lines, each with an integer qid, a question text (single word), and integer marks. Then one more line with the new question in the same 'qid text marks' form.

Output Format:
Serialize the m-question quiz, add the new question, serialize again over quiz.dat, then deserialize the file and print every stored question as 'qid text marks', followed by 'Saved: true' when the file holds exactly m + 1 questions.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 19; qid values 1..999 and the new qid is unique; text is 1 to 20 letters; 1 <= marks <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= m <= 19; unique qids 1..999; text 1..20 letters; 1 <= marks <= 100
questions.output3:
7 q7 7
8 q8 8
9 q9 9
11 q11 11
Saved: true

questions.title: Quoted Echo Printer
questions.description:
Print a word wrapped in real double quote characters. Build the quote marks from a char that holds the quote character, then also report the word length.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word.

Output Format:
Line 1: the word wrapped in double quotes, for example "Java"
Line 2: Length: <number of characters in the word>

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 30

questions.title: Quotient with Finally Cleanup
questions.description:
A finally block runs no matter what happened inside the try. Read two integers a and b and print their quotient inside try, catch a zero divisor in catch, and always print the cleanup line from finally — once on success and once after an error.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
First print 'Quotient: q' (or 'Error: Division by zero' when b is zero). Then always print 'Cleanup done'.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput2:
Error: Division by zero
Cleanup done

questions.title: Read and Print a Matrix
questions.description:
Write a program that reads a matrix and prints it back exactly. Read two integers r and c, then read r rows of c space-separated integers into a 2D array, and print the matrix row by row with values separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
r lines, each containing the c values of that row separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 100, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Rectangle Area and Perimeter
questions.description:
One rectangle object, two measurements. Define a class Rectangle with fields length and width and two methods: area() returning length * width and perimeter() returning 2 * (length + width). In main, read the two values, fill a Rectangle object, and print both results using the object's methods.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: length and width.

Output Format:
Line 1: Area: <area with 2 decimals>
Line 2: Perimeter: <perimeter with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 < length, width <= 10000

questions.title: Rectangle Area with a Class
questions.description:
OOP starts by bundling data and behavior together. Define a class Rectangle with two fields length and width and a method area() that returns length * width. In main, read the two values, store them in a Rectangle object, and print the area returned by the object's method.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: length and width.

Output Format:
Print one line: the rectangle area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < length, width <= 10000

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci Term
questions.description:
Write a recursive method fib that returns the nth term of the Fibonacci sequence defined as fib(1) = 1, fib(2) = 1 and fib(n) = fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2). Read n in main and print the nth term. Use plain recursion with the two base cases, no arrays and no loops.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the nth Fibonacci term.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 25

questions.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
questions.description:
A warehouse stores product IDs in non-decreasing (sorted) order. Compact the array in place with the two-pointer technique so each ID appears exactly once while keeping the sorted order; do not use any collection classes. Print the new length L on the first line, and the first L elements of the compacted array on the second line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of IDs.
Line 2: n space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.

Output Format:
Line 1: L, the number of distinct IDs.
Line 2: the first L elements after compaction, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= id <= 1000000000, the input array is non-decreasing

questions.title: Remove by Index and by Value
questions.description:
An ArrayList<Integer> has two remove overloads: remove(int index) deletes the element stored at that index, while remove(Object) deletes the first occurrence of that value. With Integer lists, pass Integer.valueOf(v) to remove by value. Read n integers, then remove the element at index idx, print the list, then remove the first occurrence of value val and print the list again.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: idx. Fourth line: val.

Output Format:
First line: 'Index removal: ' followed by the list after removing index idx. Second line: 'Value removal: ' followed by the list after also removing the first occurrence of val.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= idx < n; val is guaranteed to appear in the list after the index removal
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= idx < n; val appears in the list after the index removal

questions.title: Rental Bike Inherited Specs
questions.description:
A rental shop lists each bike's specs; the shared fields come from the parent class. Define class Vehicle with fields brand (String) and wheels (int). Define class Bike that extends Vehicle with an extra field gears and a method specs() that prints Brand: <brand>, Wheels: <wheels> and Gears: <gears> on three lines. In main, read brand, wheels and gears into a Bike object and call specs().

Input Format:
A single line with three values: brand wheels gears (brand is one word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Brand: <brand>
Line 2: Wheels: <wheels>
Line 3: Gears: <gears>

Constraints:
1 <= brand length <= 30, 1 <= wheels <= 4, 1 <= gears <= 10

questions.title: Replace All Occurrences of a Letter
questions.description:
Read a word, an original character and a replacement character. Print the word with every occurrence of the original character replaced by the replacement character. Use the replace method that takes two characters (no regular expressions).

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: the word, the character to replace, and the replacement character.

Output Format:
Print one line: the modified word.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, all characters are lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Report Copy Covariant Return
questions.description:
A document editor duplicates documents. Base class Doc has copy() returning a Doc with the same text. Report extends Doc with an author field and overrides copy() with a covariant return type Report, copying both fields, so the caller receives a Report directly without a cast. Read the kind and data, copy the object and print the copy's contents.

Input Format:
One line: kind text for doc, or kind text author for report (single-word values).

Output Format:
For report: Copied report: text by author. For doc: Copied doc: text.

Constraints:
kind is report or doc; 1 <= text, author length <= 30
questions.inputconstrains: kind is report or doc; 1 <= text, author length <= 30

questions.title: Report Extended With Super
questions.description:
A report generator prints a basic header, and the student version extends that behaviour. Class Report has print(String name) that prints Name: name. StudentReport overrides print with the same signature, first calling super.print(name) and then printing Role: Student. Read the kind and name and call the matching version.

Input Format:
One line: kind name where kind is student or plain.

Output Format:
Always Name: name. For student, a second line Role: Student.

Constraints:
kind is student or plain; 1 <= name length <= 30
questions.inputconstrains: kind is student or plain; 1 <= name length <= 30

questions.title: Report Template Pipeline
questions.description:
A report engine uses the template method pattern: the abstract parent fixes the pipeline, subclasses fill in the steps. Define an abstract class Report with abstract methods header() and body() and a concrete method generate() that calls header(), then body(), then prints: Report complete. Define SalesReport that extends Report printing Sales header / Sales figures, and HrReport that extends Report printing HR header / HR records. In main read n and then n kind words (sales or hr); store each matching Report object in an array using a Report reference, then call generate() on all of them in order.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n words separated by spaces, each sales or hr.

Output Format:
For each report, its header line, its body line, then Report complete.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, each kind is sales or hr
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100, each kind is sales or hr

questions.title: Reverse Lines From File
questions.description:
A review tool flips a small script file: the last written line must be shown first. Store the lines in lines.txt, then read the file back into an array and print the lines in reverse order.

Input Format:
First line: n. Then n lines of text.

Output Format:
Write the n lines to lines.txt in input order, then read them back and print line n first and line 1 last.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10 and each line has length 1 to 40

questions.title: Reverse a Word Using Recursion
questions.description:
Write a recursive method reverse that returns the reverse of a word using recursion: reverse(s) equals reverse of s without its first character, followed by that first character. The base case is a word of length 0 or 1, which is already its own reverse. Read the word in main and print the reversed word. Do not use StringBuilder and do not use loops.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the reversed word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 2000

questions.title: Right-Angled Star Triangle
questions.description:
For the school's annual day banner, print a right-angled star triangle with n rows: row i (1-based) contains exactly i star characters. Build it with nested for loops, printing the stars of each row and then moving to the next line.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
n lines; line i contains i star characters.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Robots Created Counter
questions.description:
A robot factory wants to know how many robots exist at any moment. Define a class Robot with a static int field count starting at 0; every time a new Robot object is created the count increases by 1, because the counter belongs to the class itself and is shared by every object. In main, read n commands: NEW followed by a one-word name creates one Robot, COUNT prints the current value of the shared counter.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n commands, each written as NEW (followed by a one-word name) or COUNT.

Output Format:
Print one line for every COUNT command: the number of robots created so far.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
questions.sampleinput1: 6 NEW R2 COUNT NEW R5 COUNT NEW R9 COUNT
questions.input1: 4 COUNT NEW X NEW Y COUNT
questions.input3: 6 NEW A NEW B COUNT NEW C COUNT

questions.title: Rock Paper Scissors Match
questions.description:
Two players compete at rock paper scissors. Each round is given as a two-character token: the first character is player A's move and the second is player B's move, using uppercase R, P and S. Rock beats scissors, paper beats rock and scissors beat paper. For each round print A, B or Draw; a token that is not exactly two valid move characters prints Invalid round and is skipped without scoring. The match ends early the moment either player reaches 2 wins, ignoring any remaining rounds. Afterwards print the result line: A wins the match 2-x or B wins the match x-2 when someone reached 2 wins, otherwise Match drawn a-b with the final scores.

Input Format:
First line: integer n, the number of scheduled rounds. Next n lines: one token per round.

Output Format:
One line per processed round (A, B, Draw or Invalid round), then the final result line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; each round token has 1 to 2 characters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 20; each round token has 1 to 2 characters

A wins the match 2-0
questions.sampleoutput2:

B wins the match 0-2
questions.output1:
B
Invalid round
A
Invalid round
A
A wins the match 2-1
questions.output3:

B wins the match 0-2

questions.title: Rotate the Matrix 90 Degrees Clockwise
questions.description:
A photo rotation feature turns a square image 90 degrees clockwise: the last row of the original, read left to right, becomes the first column of the result; equivalently, the element at row i, column j moves to row j, column r-1-i. Read r and c (r = c), then the r x c pixel matrix into a 2D array, fill a second 2D array with the rotated values, and print the result row by row with values separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c with r = c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
r lines, each with the c values of the rotated matrix separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= r = c <= 100, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Rotation Check
questions.description:
A cryptography workshop studies circular shifts of words. Word s2 is a rotation of word s1 when s2 can be produced by moving some prefix of s1 to its end; for example cdab is a rotation of abcd but acdb is not, and an identical word counts as a rotation (shift of zero). Check it by testing whether s2 appears inside s1 concatenated with itself, with equal lengths required.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated words, each without spaces.

Output Format:
Print yes when s2 is a rotation of s1, otherwise print no.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 100000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Row Sums of a Matrix
questions.description:
Write a program that reads a matrix and prints the sum of each row. Read r and c, then the r x c matrix, and print one line per row containing that row's sum.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
r lines, line i containing the sum of row i.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 100, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Run-Length Encoding of a Word
questions.description:
A compression module encodes test words using run-length encoding: each maximal run of one repeated character is replaced by the character followed by the length of the run, and a run of length 1 is written as just the character with no count. For example aaabb becomes a3b2 and abbc becomes ab2c. Read the word and print its encoded form, building the answer with StringBuilder.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the run-length encoded word.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Runner-Up Score Hunt
questions.description:
A gaming leaderboard stores n scores. Without sorting the array, use enhanced for loops to find the champion score and then the best score that is strictly below it (the runner-up). If every score is identical, the runner-up does not exist.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the scores.

Output Format:
One line with the runner-up score, or the single line No second place when all scores are equal.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= score <= 1000000000

questions.title: Saddle Point Search in a Grid
questions.description:
A quality inspector looks for a saddle point in a hardness grid: a value that is the minimum of its row and at the same time the maximum of its column. Read r and c, then the r x c grid. Print three space-separated numbers: the 1-based row, the 1-based column and the value of the first saddle point found scanning rows top to bottom and columns left to right. If no saddle point exists, print -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: two space-separated integers r and c.
Next r lines: c space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
One line: row, column and value separated by single spaces, or -1 if there is no saddle point.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 100, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Safe Addition Auditor
questions.description:
A banking batch job adds two large transaction values stored as long, and adding blindly can overflow the long range. Read two long values, print them, then audit the sum: overflow happens when both values are positive and their sum would exceed the maximum long, or when both are negative and their sum would go below the minimum long. Print the safe sum with status OK, or the overflow report.

Input Format:
One line with two long integers separated by a space.

Output Format:
When safe:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: <a + b>
Status: OK
When overflowing:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807

Constraints:
a and b are any two 64 bit long values
