questions.title: Safe Division Checker
questions.description:
Division by zero crashes a program with an ArithmeticException. Read two integers a and b, then print their integer quotient. If b is zero, catch the ArithmeticException and print a friendly error message instead of letting the program crash.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print 'Result: q' where q is a divided by b (integer division). If b is zero, print 'Error: Division by zero'.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000

questions.title: Safe Grade Mapper
questions.description:
A teacher portal converts numeric scores into letter grades, but students sometimes type nonsense like 'abc'. NumberFormatException is an unchecked exception, so the compiler never forces you to handle it — catching it anyway keeps the portal alive. Read one score token and map it: 90 or more prints A, 75 to 89 prints B, 60 to 74 prints C, and anything below 60 prints D.

Input Format:
A single token: a score, or any non-numeric token.

Output Format:
Print 'Grade: X' where X is one of A, B, C, D for a valid integer. Print 'Invalid score' when the token cannot be parsed as an int.

Constraints:
The token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Safe Matrix Cell Reader
questions.description:
A heatmap dashboard reads one requested cell of a matrix. Accessing a row or column outside the matrix throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; catch it and report a clear message instead of crashing.

Input Format:
First line: r and c. Next r lines: c space-separated integers each. Last line: i and j, the requested cell.

Output Format:
Print 'Cell: value' for a valid cell. Otherwise print 'Error: Cell out of bounds'.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 20 and each cell value satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

questions.title: Salary Bonus With Nested Ternaries
questions.description:
A company pays an annual bonus decided by rating and service years, coded as one nested ternary expression (if statements are forbidden): rating 1 earns 20 percent for 5 or more years of service, otherwise 15 percent; rating 2 earns 12 percent for 5 or more years, otherwise 8 percent; rating 3 always earns 5 percent. Also report the truncated whole-rupee monthly hike.

Input Format:
One line: salary (decimal number), years (integer) and rating (1 to 3), space separated.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Bonus: X' with X to exactly 2 decimals. Line 2: 'New salary: Y' with Y to exactly 2 decimals. Line 3: 'Monthly hike: N' where N is (int) (bonus / 12).

Constraints:
1000 <= salary <= 1000000; 0 <= years <= 40; rating is 1, 2 or 3.

questions.title: Save Employee Snapshot
questions.description:
An HR tool snapshots one employee record to disk using object serialization: an Employee object (a Serializable class defined in the same file, also Comparable by salary) is written with ObjectOutputStream into employee.dat.

Input Format:
One line with the employee name (single word) and integer salary separated by a space.

Output Format:
After serializing, print 'Saved: name salary' from the object, then print 'File exists: true' by checking a File object for employee.dat.

Constraints:
Name is a single word of 1 to 20 letters; 1000 <= salary <= 1000000

questions.title: Savings Goal with Monthly Interest
questions.description:
Aarav opens a savings account with an initial balance and deposits a fixed amount at the start of every month. At the end of each month the bank adds 2 percent interest, computed with integer math as balance = balance + balance * 2 / 100. Simulate month by month with a while loop until the balance reaches or exceeds the target, then report the number of months needed and the final balance (if the initial balance already meets the target, 0 months pass).

Input Format:
One line with three integers: initial balance, monthly deposit, and target.

Output Format:
Line 1: the number of months needed.
Line 2: the final balance.

Constraints:
1 <= initial <= 10000, 1 <= deposit <= 1000, 1 <= target <= 1000000

questions.title: School Introduction Override
questions.description:
At a school assembly every person introduces themselves differently. Base class Person has introduce() printing a plain hello. Student overrides it to mention the grade and Teacher overrides it to mention the subject. Read the role and details, create the matching object and call its overridden introduce().

Input Format:
One line starting with role: student name grade, teacher name subject, or guest name.

Output Format:
Student: Hi, I am name from grade g. Teacher: Hello, I am name, teacher of subject. Guest: Hello, I am name.

Constraints:

Line 2: Roll: <rollNo>
Line 3: Marks: <marks>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50, 1 <= rollNo <= 9999, 0 <= marks <= 100

Line 1: student name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: starting day (an integer)

Output Format:
Student: <name>
Plan: Day <start> to Day <end>
Days completed: <completed>
Days remaining: <30 - end>

Constraints:
1 <= start <= 29, 1 <= completed, start + completed <= 30

questions.title: Sum Integers From File
questions.description:
A sensor dumps integers into a file, one per line, and a report later reads the file back to total them. Write each input integer to nums.txt on its own line, then reopen the file, read every line back, and print the sum.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Print 'Sum: s' where s is the sum of all integers read back from nums.txt.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000 and -1000000 <= each value <= 1000000

questions.title: Sum Until Zero Skipping Negatives
questions.description:
A data-entry clerk totals a batch of sensor readings. Positive values are added to a running sum and counted; negative readings are skipped with continue; a zero reading stops processing immediately with break and everything after it is ignored. Read n values and print the final sum and count of the positive values that were processed.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sum of the processed positive values. Line 2: the count of the processed positive values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Sum Until the Zero Sentinel
questions.description:
A cashier terminal accepts integers one by one until the sentinel value 0 appears; the 0 ends the session and is not counted as a sale. Read the values with a do-while loop and print the sum of all values before the sentinel.

Input Format:
A sequence of integers terminated by 0 (the final 0 ends the input).

Output Format:
One line with the sum of all values before the sentinel.

Constraints:
1 to 1000 values before the sentinel 0, each between -10000 and 10000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 to 1000 values before the sentinel 0, each between -10000 and 10000

questions.title: Sum and Average of Array Elements
questions.description:
Read n integers into an array, then compute the total of all elements and their average. Print the total on the first line and the average rounded to exactly 2 decimal places on the second line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the sum of all elements.
Line 2: the average rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= element <= 1000000

questions.title: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
questions.description:
Read an integer n and print the sum of all natural numbers from 1 to n using a for loop.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line containing the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Sum of First N in a Runnable
questions.description:
A Runnable describes the work; a Thread executes it. Read one integer n, create an anonymous class implementing Runnable whose run() method computes the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n into a shared field, wrap it in a Thread, start it, and join() it before printing. join() guarantees the computation finished.

Input Format:
A single line with one integer n.

Output Format:
One line: 'Sum: s' where s = 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Sum of N Natural Numbers Recursively
questions.description:
Write a recursive method sumNatural that returns the sum of the first n natural numbers (1 + 2 + ... + n) using recursion only, with no loops. The base case returns 0 for n = 0. Read n in main and print the returned sum.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the recursive sum 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Super Show Extended Profile
questions.description:
super.method() lets a subclass reuse the parent's behavior and then add its own. Define class Employee with a field name and a method show() that prints: Profile: <name>. Define class Developer that extends Employee and overrides show() to first call super.show() and then print: Skills: Java. In main, read the name into a Developer object and call show().

Input Format:
A single line with one word: the employee name.

Output Format:
Line 1: Profile: <name>
Line 2: Skills: Java

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50 (single word)

questions.title: Supplier Shape Factory
questions.description:
A shape toolkit computes measurements lazily through factories. Define a generic method declared as public static <T> T produce(Supplier<T> factory) and build the chosen shape's formula as a Supplier<Double> lambda, then invoke it through produce. Use if-else selection, not a switch statement.

Input Format:
One line: a shape (circle, square or cube) and a decimal size (radius for circle, side for square and cube).

Output Format:
Print 'Label: v' with v to 2 decimals, where Label is 'Circle area' (pi*r*r), 'Square area' (s*s) or 'Cube volume' (s*s*s).

Constraints:
0 < size <= 1000

questions.title: Swap Attempt and Call by Value
questions.description:
Java always passes arguments by value. Write a program that demonstrates this: a static method attemptSwap receives two integers as parameters, swaps its local copies, and prints them in the form Inside method: X Y. After the call, main prints the original variables in the form Original values: A B. The originals must remain unchanged because the method only swapped copies.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Line 1: Inside method: Y X (the swapped copies inside the method)
Line 2: Original values: a b (the unchanged originals in main)

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000

questions.title: Sweep Out the Negatives
questions.description:
A sensor writes temperature readings to a list, but faulty sensors produce negative junk values. Clean the list with a single pass using an Iterator: every negative reading must be removed through it.remove() (never through the list's own remove method, which would corrupt the iteration). Report the cleaned list and how many readings were removed.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
First line: 'Cleaned: ' followed by the surviving values space-separated in order. Second line: 'Removed: ' followed by the count of removed readings.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; -1000000 <= reading <= 1000000

questions.title: Synchronized Hit Counter
questions.description:
A website counts hits arriving from several visitors at once. Without synchronization the shared counter loses updates. Read m (visitor threads) and n (hits per visitor); each thread increments one shared counter n times through a static synchronized method. Start all threads, join them all, then print the final count, which must be exactly m * n.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers m and n.

Output Format:
One line: 'Final count: c' where c = m * n.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 5, 1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Task Scheduler Runs Jobs By Priority
questions.description:
A continuous integration server runs pending jobs one at a time; every job has a name and a priority number, and a smaller priority number means the job runs earlier. All priorities are distinct. Read every job, put the priorities into a PriorityQueue, then simulate execution by repeatedly polling the smallest priority and printing the name of the job that carries it.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name priority where name is a single word and all priorities are distinct.

Output Format:
One line per executed job: the job name, in execution order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500; priorities are distinct integers with 1 <= priority <= 1000000

questions.title: Temperature Converter Suite
questions.description:
A weather dashboard converts temperatures between scales. Build the three converters as Function<Double, Double> lambdas (c2f: v*9/5+32, f2c: (v-32)*5/9, k2c: v-273.15) and apply the one named in the input.

Input Format:
One line: a decimal value and a mode (c2f, f2c or k2c).

Output Format:
Print the converted value with exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Temperature Min and Max in One Pass
questions.description:
A weather station logged n temperature readings for the day. Using a single enhanced for loop pass (no sorting, no Math.max or Math.min), find the lowest and the highest reading.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the readings.

Output Format:
Line 1: Min: <lowest reading>
Line 2: Max: <highest reading>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, each reading between -50 and 60

questions.title: Temperature Sensor Copy
questions.description:
A weather station keeps a live Sensor reading and a backup copy created with a copy constructor. Calibration later shifts only the backup by an offset. Define class Sensor with field reading, a parameterized constructor Sensor(int reading), and a copy constructor Sensor(Sensor other) that copies the reading. Read the reading and the offset; create the live sensor, create the backup with the copy constructor, add the offset to the backup's reading, then print both.

Input Format:
One line: reading offset (both integers).

Output Format:
Line 1: Sensor: <live reading>
Line 2: Backup: <backup reading>

Constraints:
-50 <= reading <= 150, 0 <= offset <= 50

questions.title: Thermostat Setter Validation
questions.description:
A smart thermostat accepts temperatures only inside a safe window. Define a class Thermostat with a private double field celsius starting at 20.0, a method setTemperature(double t) that stores t only when 10 <= t <= 35 and otherwise prints Out of range while keeping the old value, a method getCelsius(), and a method report() that prints two lines: Celsius: <celsius with 2 decimals> and Fahrenheit: <celsius * 9 / 5 + 32 with 2 decimals>. In main, read n operations: S t sets the temperature, P reports it.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter S followed by a number, or the letter P alone.

Output Format:
Print Out of range for every rejected S; for every P print the two lines described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -50 <= t <= 150

A fresh thread object sits in the NEW state until start() is called, and once its run() method has finished and join() has returned it is TERMINATED. A single line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Three lines: 'State before start: NEW', 'State after join: TERMINATED' and 'Double: d' where d = 2 * n.

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5

questions.title: Throws Propagation Chain
questions.description:
Instead of catching an exception where it occurs, a method can declare it with throws and let it propagate up the call chain until some caller handles it. Here parse(token) declares NumberFormatException, divide(a, b) declares NumberFormatException and ArithmeticException, and only main catches — one catch of RuntimeException covering both unchecked types. Print the result, or let main report the exception's own message.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated tokens a and b.

Output Format:
Print 'Result: q' when both tokens parse and b is nonzero. Otherwise print 'Handled in main: message' where message is the exception's getMessage() — for example / by zero (zero divisor) or For input string: "abc" (bad token).

Constraints:
Each token has length between 1 and 20.

Input Format:
3 lines, each exactly 3 characters: X, O or -.

Output Format:
3 lines. Line i contains the 3 characters of row i separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
Exactly 3 lines of exactly 3 characters each; only characters X, O and -

questions.description:
A concert counter builds a Ticket object for every sale, and the parameterized constructor itself does all the pricing: a VIP ticket costs 250 and a Regular ticket costs 100, and the constructor computes total = unitPrice * quantity. Define class Ticket with fields category, quantity, unitPrice and total, and a constructor Ticket(String category, int quantity) that stores category and quantity, decides unitPrice from the category, and computes total. Read category and quantity, create the ticket, and print the stored values.

One line: category quantity (category is the word VIP or Regular).

Output Format:

category is VIP or Regular, 0 <= quantity <= 100

questions.title: Tip Calculator Method
questions.description:
A restaurant app computes tips with a static method tipAmount that receives the bill amount and the tip rate as parameters and returns the tip as bill * rate / 100.0. In main, read the bill and the rate, call the method, and print two lines: first the tip, then the total (bill plus tip), both rounded to 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: bill and rate (rate is a percentage, e.g. 10 means 10 percent).

Output Format:
Line 1: the tip rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 2: the total (bill plus tip) rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= bill <= 100000, 0 <= rate <= 50

questions.title: Token Queue in Reverse Order
questions.description:
A clinic issues token numbers to patients in arrival order and stores them in an array. The display board above the door shows the latest token first, so the receptionist needs the token list printed in reverse order (last issued first). Print the tokens on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of tokens issued.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the token numbers in issue order.

Output Format:
One line with the token numbers in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= token <= 999999

questions.title: Toll Gate Revenue Lock
questions.description:
A toll gate uses an explicit ReentrantLock instead of the synchronized keyword so reviewers can see exactly where the gate is locked and unlocked. Read m (cars), n (trips per car) and f (fee per trip). Every trip passes through the locked section once: revenue grows by f and the vehicle counter grows by 1. Join all car threads, then print total revenue and vehicles served.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers m, n and f.

Output Format:
Two lines: 'Total revenue: r' where r = m * n * f, and 'Vehicles served: p' where p = m * n.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 5, 1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= f <= 100

questions.title: Top-K Most Requested Items
questions.description:
A server logs the ids of requested items. Find the k most requested distinct ids: rank by request count descending, and break ties by whichever id appeared earlier in the log. Count requests without any key-value map: sort a copy of the log, walk its runs to get each distinct id and its count, and find each id's first-appearance position with an index scan of the original log.

Input Format:
First line: n and k space-separated. Second line: n space-separated integers (the log).

Output Format:
One line: 'Top: ' followed by the k ids, most requested first, ties broken by first appearance, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 4000; k <= number of distinct ids; -1000000 <= id <= 1000000

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Move Count Recursively
questions.description:
A puzzle shop ships the classic Tower of Hanoi and must print the exact minimum number of moves for n discs on the instruction sheet. Write a recursive method hanoiMoves(n) using the relation hanoiMoves(n) = 2 * hanoiMoves(n - 1) + 1 with the base case hanoiMoves(1) = 1. Math.pow is banned, build the count purely by recursion.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n, the number of discs.

Output Format:
Print one line: the minimum number of moves for n discs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Transient Session Reset

A login service caches user sessions, but security policy forbids persisting tokens: the sessionToken field of User is declared transient, so the serialization engine skips it. After the user list (Serializable, Comparable by name) is saved to users.dat and loaded back, every session token has reverted to its default value (null).

Serialize the list to users.dat, deserialize it back, and for each user print 'name role' on one line and 'Session: token' on the next — the deserialized token is always null because the field is transient. Finally print 'Count: n'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20 and every word has 1 to 15 letters

One line with three space-separated integers a, b and c.

Print Invalid triangle, Equilateral, Isosceles or Scalene.

1 <= a, b, c <= 1000

questions.title: Trip Expense Splitter

Four friends went on a trek and paid one total bill. They split the cost equally; whatever cannot be divided evenly stays as leftover rupees.

One line with two space-separated integers: the total cost in rupees and the number of friends.

Output Format:
Print two lines: 'Each pays: X' where X is the integer share per friend, then 'Left over: Y' where Y is the remaining rupees.

1 <= cost <= 1000000 and 1 <= friends <= 100.

questions.title: Two Catch Blocks Selector

One try can be followed by several catch blocks, each handling a different exception type. Read two tokens, convert both to integers, and print their quotient. questions.title: Two File Interleaver

questions.title: Two Integer Arithmetic Drill

questions.title: Visitor Log Dedupe

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated names.

Output Format:
First line: 'Unique: ' followed by the deduplicated names space-separated in first-appearance order. Second line: 'Count: ' followed by the number of unique names.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; names are single words of length 1 to 20

6
ann bob ann cid bob ella

questions.title: Vowel or Consonant Check
questions.description:
A phonics app listens to single letters spoken by children and reacts differently for vowels. Read one lowercase English letter and decide whether it is a vowel or a consonant.

Input Format:
A single lowercase letter.

Output Format:
Print Vowel for a, e, i, o or u; otherwise print Consonant.

Constraints:
The input is exactly one lowercase letter from a to z

questions.title: Walk Both Ways with ListIterator
questions.description:
A media player keeps its upcoming queue in a list. The review screen shows the queue twice: once from front to back and once from back to front. Use a ListIterator for both passes: walk forward with hasNext and next, then walk backward with hasPrevious and previous starting from the same iterator position (the end).

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated words (queue items).

Output Format:
First line: 'Forward: ' followed by the items space-separated front to back. Second line: 'Backward: ' followed by the items space-separated back to front.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; each word has length 1 to 20

questions.title: Wallet Deposit Withdraw
questions.description:
An encapsulated wallet never exposes its money directly. Define a class Wallet with a private double field balance, a method deposit(double amount), a method withdraw(double amount) that subtracts only when amount <= balance and otherwise prints Insufficient funds, a method printBalance() that prints Balance: <balance with 2 decimals>, and a method getBalance(). In main, read n operations and apply them in order on one Wallet object: D amount deposits, W amount withdraws, P prints the current balance. After all operations print Final: <balance with 2 decimals> using getBalance().

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by an amount, or the letter P alone.

Output Format:
For every P print Balance: <balance with 2 decimals>; print Insufficient funds immediately for every rejected withdrawal; at the end print Final: <balance with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000

m lines 'Loader i carried: w' in loader order, then 'Total weight: t'.

questions.title: Warehouse Stock Auditor
questions.description:

questions.title: Weekly Temperature Day Averages
questions.description:
A weather station stores its readings in a grid: one row per week and one column per day. The first line contains two integers: n (the number of weeks) and d (the number of days per week, d = 7). Then follow n lines, each with d space-separated integers (line i holds the temperatures of week i, column j holds day j). Line 1: two space-separated integers n and d (d = 7).
Next n lines: d space-separated integers each.

d lines, each the average of one day column across all weeks with exactly 2 decimal places.

1 <= n <= 20, d = 7, -50 <= temperature <= 50

questions.title: Which Word Comes First
questions.description:
Read two words and decide their dictionary (lexicographic) order using compareTo. Print first if the first word comes earlier in dictionary order, second if the second word comes earlier, or equal if the words are identical.

questions.title: Worker State Trail
questions.description:
A QA script audits a worker thread's lifecycle states while it processes a small batch: main observes the fresh object before start(), the worker reports its own state before and after a short sleep, and main reports the state after join(). A single line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Five lines: 'Main sees before start: NEW', 'Worker sees before sleep: RUNNABLE', 'Worker sees after sleep: RUNNABLE', 'Main sees after join: TERMINATED' and 'Sum: s' where s = 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
